question.html:
A sample of Polonium-210 emits alpha particles () with a kinetic energy of . These particles are collimated into a beam that enters a vacuum chamber. In the chamber, the particles encounter a uniform magnetic field and a uniform electric field, which are oriented such that the forces they exert on the alpha particles are in opposite directions.

a Determine the velocity of the alpha particles released from the source, given that each particle carries a kinetic energy of . [2]

b A uniform magnetic field of is applied perpendicular to the path of the alpha particles. Calculate the strength of the electric field required to maintain the particles on a linear trajectory, and describe the required orientation of this electric field relative to the magnetic field and the particle velocity. [3]

c Demonstrate that the time taken for an alpha particle to complete one full circular orbit in this magnetic field (the orbital period ) is independent of its initial speed. [1]

d If the electric field is deactivated, calculate the radius of the circular path followed by the alpha particles in the magnetic field. [2]

e The beam is found to contain helium-3 nuclei () alongside the alpha particles. Assuming both types of ions possess the same kinetic energy of , explain, with reference to their radius of curvature, how the magnetic field can be used to separate these two isotopes in a mass spectrometer. [3]
